title: When the Volunteer Hours Were Too High
script: Arman: [thoughtful] Zaki, the certificate says I volunteered for sixty hours, but my own record shows forty-six.
Zaki: Maybe the coordinator included travel and preparation time.
Arman: [gently] I included preparation already. Even with travel, it would not reach sixty.
Zaki: Do you need the certificate for your job application?
Arman: [carefully] Yes, and sixty hours looks better. That is why correcting it feels difficult.
Zaki: If you submit a number you believe is wrong, the certificate does not make it honest.
Arman: [reflective] I know. I should ask how they calculated it before assuming the coordinator made a careless mistake.
Zaki: Exactly. Send your dates and ask for a breakdown.
Arman: [honestly] What if their policy counts all event days as five hours, even when we left early?
Zaki: Then explain your actual attendance. A standard system can still produce an inaccurate individual total.
Arman: [warmly] I do not want the coordinator to think I am ungrateful.
Zaki: You can thank her for the certificate and say you want your application to be accurate.
Arman: [sincere] I will attach my log: eight events, planning meetings, and home preparation.
Zaki: Keep the message simple. You do not need to accuse anyone.
Arman: If they confirm forty-six, I will request a corrected certificate.
Zaki: And if they show valid hours you missed in your record, you can update yours.
Arman: That is fair. The goal is the true number, not the lower number.
Zaki: Right. Honesty does not mean automatically choosing what harms you. It means accepting verified facts.
Arman: I will send the question today, before I upload the application.
Zaki: Good. Correcting a flattering error protects your work from becoming a claim you cannot defend.

quiz.question: What conflict does Arman find?
options: The certificate says sixty hours, his log says forty-six
quiz.explanation: Two records show different volunteer totals.

quiz.question: Why is correction difficult?
options: The larger number improves his application
quiz.explanation: Personal benefit creates a test of honesty.

quiz.question: What should he request first?
quiz.explanation: He needs facts before claiming an error.

quiz.question: What evidence will he send?
quiz.explanation: His own record supports a respectful review.

quiz.question: What does Zaki say honesty means?
options: Accepting verified facts, not automatically choosing less
Using any official document without question
quiz.explanation: The goal is an accurate defensible total.

quiz.question: Why does Arman not immediately demand forty-six hours?
options: He wants to hide all volunteering
The coordinator may have valid counted time missing from his log
quiz.explanation: He seeks the verified number, not a preferred number.

quiz.question: What tone should Arman use?
quiz.explanation: A calculation question can be respectful.

quiz.question: What does the personal log provide?
options: Dates and activities that can be compared with the certificate
Proof that every event lasted five hours

quiz.question: When should Arman upload the certificate?
options: Before checking because sixty looks better
Only if the hours are reduced
After asking for and resolving the calculation
quiz.explanation: He avoids making a claim he already doubts.

quiz.question: What broader principle does the dialogue teach?
options: Honesty always selects the smaller number
Honesty follows verified facts even when an error flatters us
quiz.explanation: Truth is neither self-serving nor automatically self-harming.
